A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CVaR-VaR research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments in Maze, LunarLander, and InvertedPendulum, including return, risk-averse behavior, and CVaR learning curves.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and their results in Figures 2–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 4 corrects the stated policy update from g1 + g2 to (1−ω)g1 + ωg2. The objective also switches ω from weighting CVaR to weighting expected VaR. This is a limited correction to the reported update specification; the architecture, Bellman operators, risk-level tracking, and multi-step estimators remain unchanged. Implementation changes or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same modified Maze, LunarLander, and InvertedPendulum tasks with identical noisy-reward regions and risk-averse behavioral requirements. No additional domains or test scenarios appear in the appendices.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain REINFORCE, CVaR-PG, PCVaR-PG, RET-CAP, and MIX, with the same participation by task. MIX remains excluded from Maze, and unsuccessful PCVaR-PG results remain omitted from the LunarLander plots.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix C retain the same evaluation metrics, episode limits, risk levels, 20-trajectory update batches, network sizes, and hyperparameter tables. The numerical ω schedules are also unchanged; the weighting-specification correction is described under M1.

E4.justification: No ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests, or supplementary empirical analyses are added or removed. The new appendix material concerns theoretical guarantees rather than additional experiments.

E5.justification: Figures 2–3 report averages over 10 seeds with shaded standard errors in both versions. No new repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 contain identical learning-curve graphics, and Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same performance trends, rankings, and baseline failure findings. There are no new empirical result entries in the appendices.

T1.justification: New Appendices A.5–A.6 establish contraction and fixed-point results for policy evaluation, define a loss-induced risk measure, and prove monotone policy improvement under finite-action, bounded-reward, softmax-policy, and step-size conditions. These substantive guarantees were absent from v1. The earlier proofs are largely retained, with the Proposition 3.4 proof moved to A.7.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: augmenting Markovian CVaR policy optimization with quantile gradients to improve sample efficiency and risk-averse performance. The new proofs strengthen support without redefining these headline claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds a variance-based rationale for state-value advantages and explains consistent tie-breaking when optimal policies are nonunique. Section 3.3 newly interprets decaying ω as removing the VaR boost and asserts recovery of CVaR-PG's convergence properties. The unresolved convergence of the general Markovian learner remains acknowledged.

D1.justification: Algorithm 4 now explicitly applies the gradient-mixing weights that v1 omitted from its pseudocode, improving implementation clarity. The new tie-breaking note also clarifies policy execution. Appendix C's architectures, learning parameters, preprocessing details, and environment-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Föllmer and Schied (2016), Agarwal et al. (2021), and Schulman et al. (2017), supporting CVaR equivalence, policy-gradient analysis, and the state-value rationale. A Langley (2000) bibliography entry is also added. The positioning relative to existing CVaR methods remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Local explanations in Section 3 are expanded, acknowledgements and an impact statement are added, affiliation information changes, and references move from after the appendices to before them.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference-style main text and bibliography with running headers. Existing figures are resized and relocated, algorithms are reflowed, and Tables 1–3 are regrouped onto one page. The underlying figure graphics and table contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v1 introduced VaR actor–critic updates without the policy-evaluation and policy-improvement guarantees supplied by v3's Appendices A.5–A.6. These additions substantially strengthen the mathematical foundation, while the corrected mixing weights resolve an important inconsistency in Algorithm 4. The improvement is primarily theoretical and documentary: empirical evidence is unchanged, and the conditional guarantees do not resolve convergence of the full Markovian learner.
